title: One of Several
goal: A value that is exactly one of a few named options.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Afternoon: User-Defined Types

sections.text: An enum declares a type whose value is exactly one of a few named options, called variants. Most languages have something like this, usually as a list of constants.

sections.caption: Four variants, and heading is exactly one of them.

sections.text: Rust adds something those constant lists do not have. A variant can carry data, and each variant can carry something different.

sections.caption: Add carries a number, SetName carries text, Reset carries nothing.

sections.text: This is why enums do so much work in Rust. `Option` and `Result`, which you meet later, are just enums whose variants carry the value or the error.
Because the type lists every possibility, the compiler knows them all. That becomes useful the moment you read the value back, which is the next lecture.

explanation: A value that is exactly one of a few named options.
